title: Binary Gap
statement:
Write the positive integer `n` in binary. Call two `1` bits neighbours when every bit strictly between them is `0` (there may be no bits between them at all). The gap of a pair of neighbours is the difference of their bit positions; for instance the two `1` bits of `1001` are 3 apart.

Return the largest gap over all pairs of neighbouring `1` bits, or `0` when `n` has a single `1` bit.
notes:
## Intuition

The answer only depends on where the `1` bits are. Scanning the bits from the lowest upward, each `1` bit's neighbour on the right is simply the previous `1` bit seen, so remembering the position of the last `1` is enough. The simple alternative builds the binary string and compares positions of consecutive `'1'` characters; the bit scan does the same without a string.

## Approach

1. Set `longest = 0` and `last = -1` (no `1` bit seen yet).
2. Walk `bit = 0, 1, 2, ...` while `n > 0`, looking at the lowest bit `n & 1`.
3. When that bit is `1` and an earlier `1` exists, the gap is `bit - last`; keep the larger of it and `longest`. Then set `last = bit`.
4. Shift `n` right by one to bring the next bit into the lowest place.
5. Return `longest`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 22` is `10110`. Bit 0 is `0`. Bit 1 is `1`: first one seen, `last = 1`. Bit 2 is `1`: gap `2 - 1 = 1`, `longest = 1`, `last = 2`. Bit 3 is `0`. Bit 4 is `1`: gap `4 - 2 = 2`, `longest = 2`. Now `n` is `0`, so the answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n): one step per bit, at most 30 for `n <= 10^9`.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- A single `1` bit (a power of two) has no pair; the answer is `0`, not the number of trailing zeros.
- Only consecutive `1` bits form pairs; the gap from the lowest to the highest `1` is not the answer.
- Two adjacent `1` bits (`11`) are 1 apart, not 0.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `longest` | largest gap found so far |
| `last` | position of the previous `1` bit, or `-1` |
| `bit` | position of the bit now in the lowest place of `n` |

narration.2: No gap has been measured yet.
narration.3: -1 means no 1 bit has been seen so far.
narration.5: Visit bit positions from the lowest until no set bits remain in n.
narration.6: Is the bit at this position a 1?
narration.7: Only measure a gap if an earlier 1 bit exists.
narration.8: The distance to the previous 1 bit is a candidate for the answer.
narration.10: This 1 bit becomes the previous one for the next pair.
narration.12: Shift right so the next bit moves into the lowest place.
narration.14: Return the largest gap between neighbouring 1 bits.
